connector.name: Ccu MCP
connector.registryDescription: MCP server for controlling HomeMatic smart home devices via the CCU JSON-RPC API
connector.summary: Runs locally from the npm package ccu-mcp. Needs an API key you supply, and it reaches 8 of 9 clients tracked here.
connector.provenanceNote: Published from the claymore666 account, and the linked repository sits under the same account. Namespace ownership was proven at publish time.
connector.authNote: A long lived key or token is required. Scope it as narrowly as the upstream service allows and rotate it on a schedule.

env.name: CCU_HOST
env.description: Hostname or IP of your HomeMatic CCU (debmatic, CCU3, or OpenCCU/RaspberryMatic)

env.name: CCU_PASSWORD
env.description: CCU admin password (same as the WebUI login)

env.name: CCU_USER
env.description: CCU username

env.name: CCU_HTTPS
env.description: Connect to the CCU via HTTPS (self-signed certificates supported)

env.name: CCU_PORT
env.description: CCU API port (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS)

env.name: CACHE_DIR
env.description: Directory for the device type cache and session persistence

env.name: MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
env.description: Comma-separated allowlist of browser origins. Unset = no cross-origin browser access (default-deny). An allowlisted origin is reflected exactly in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (never '*'); the list also drives DNS-rebinding origin checks

env.name: MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS
env.description: Extra Host header values accepted by DNS-rebinding protection (comma-separated host:port); add your hostname when behind a proxy or container DNS name

env.name: CCU_PROFILES
env.description: Comma-separated names of multiple CCU targets (e.g. 'prod,dev'). Each profile takes the flat CCU_* settings prefixed CCU_<NAME>_ (CCU_PROD_HOST, ...), plus policy flags CCU_<NAME>_PROTECTED (writes need confirm:true) and CCU_<NAME>_READONLY. Unset = single default profile from the flat CCU_* vars

env.name: CCU_DEFAULT_PROFILE
env.description: Which profile from CCU_PROFILES is active at startup (default: the first listed)

env.name: CCU_TLS_VERIFY
env.description: Verify the CCU's TLS certificate against the system trust store. Only meaningful with CCU_HTTPS=true. Default false, because a CCU ships a self-signed certificate — prefer CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT or CCU_CA_CERT to verify one of those

env.name: CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT
env.description: Pin the CCU's self-signed leaf certificate by its SHA-256 fingerprint (hex, colons optional). The strongest option for an appliance: the connection is rejected unless the presented certificate matches. Takes precedence over CCU_CA_CERT

env.name: CCU_CA_CERT
env.description: Path to a PEM file holding the CCU's CA or self-signed certificate. The connection is then validated against it with standard chain verification

env.name: CCU_TIMEOUT
env.description: Timeout for a CCU JSON-RPC call, in MILLISECONDS

env.name: CCU_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT
env.description: Timeout for HomeMatic Script execution (ReGa), in MILLISECONDS — scripts are slower than plain API calls

env.name: CACHE_TTL
env.description: Lifetime of the on-disk device-type schema cache, in SECONDS

env.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_BURST
env.description: Token-bucket burst size for CCU requests — how many may be issued back to back

env.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_RATE
env.description: Sustained CCU request rate, in requests per second

env.name: RESOURCE_POLL_INTERVAL
env.description: How often MCP resources are polled for change notifications, in SECONDS

env.name: LOG_LEVEL
env.description: error | warn | info | debug. Logs are structured JSON on stderr
